about: Impact flags for the Shadowserver report types, in Looking Glass's own words (not Shadowserver's text): what each kind of exposure or event can lead to. An advisory that lists a report shows its flags. Per report where the impact is specific, else the default of its group (report_map_rules.json). Curated reference data: shipped with Looking Glass.

infected.label: Already compromised
infected.text: The device is talking to a sinkholed botnet control server or carries an implant: it is compromised now, not merely at risk.

takeover.label: Device takeover
takeover.text: An attacker can run code on the device or take full control of it.

physical.label: Physical process risk
physical.text: Industrial control equipment: tampering can disrupt physical processes, equipment or safety.

c2.label: Attacker infrastructure
c2.text: Attacker tooling (command and control, post-exploitation frameworks) runs inside the constituency.

known_vuln.label: Known vulnerability
known_vuln.text: A publicly documented flaw with fixes available; attackers scan for it automatically.

unauth.label: Unauthorised remote access
unauth.text: A service meant for administrators or internal use answers anyone on the internet.

data.label: Data exposure or theft
data.text: Stored data can be read, copied, changed or deleted, and is often held to ransom.

ransom.label: Ransomware entry point
ransom.text: One of the most common ways in for ransomware operators.

wormable.label: Wormable / spreads inside
wormable.text: Flaws in this service have been used by worms to spread from machine to machine.

botnet.label: Botnet recruitment
botnet.text: Targeted by botnets (Mirai and others) that enlist devices to attack third parties.

attacking.label: Attacking others
attacking.text: The device attacks other systems (scans, password guessing, floods), as seen by honeypots.

malicious_hosting.label: Malicious content hosted
malicious_hosting.text: Serves malware, phishing or spam links to others from the constituency.

credentials.label: Leaked credentials
credentials.text: Accounts can be taken over until their passwords are changed and sessions revoked.

bruteforce.label: Password guessing
bruteforce.text: Exposed logins are targeted by automated password guessing.

amp.label: DDoS amplification
amp.text: Can be abused to flood third parties with traffic, using the network's bandwidth and reputation.

proxy.label: Anonymised abuse
proxy.text: Others can route attacks, spam or fraud through the network.

spoofing.label: Address spoofing
spoofing.text: Forged source addresses leave the network: the basis of reflection attacks.

dos.label: Service disruption
dos.text: The service or network can be knocked offline.

weak_crypto.label: Weak encryption
weak_crypto.text: Traffic can be decrypted or tampered with on the way.

routing.label: Routing manipulation
routing.text: Routing sessions open to the internet can be disrupted or used to divert traffic.

reputation.label: Reputation damage
reputation.text: Listed addresses lose mail delivery and access to partner services.

info.label: Information disclosure
info.text: Reveals software, versions or configuration that help attackers plan.
